I can’t edit the photo directly because no image-editing tool is available here. I can, however, give clear, actionable instructions you can follow (or give to a retoucher) to remove the mug while leaving everything else unchanged. Tell me which program or app you’ll use (Photoshop, Photopea, GIMP, Snapseed, or an online inpainting tool) and I’ll tailor the steps — below are solid, general methods and tool-specific options.

General workflow (applies to most tools)
1. Work non‑destructively: duplicate the background layer / save a copy of the file first.
2. Select the mug plus a small margin of surrounding area (lasso, brush mask).
3. Use an automatic fill/inpainting tool to remove the object (Content‑Aware Fill / Heal / Inpaint). If the result isn’t perfect, use manual cloning/healing.
4. Repair any leftover seams, texture mismatches, or shadow issues with a small soft Clone Stamp / Healing Brush and sampling nearby clean areas.
5. Recreate or refine shadows if the mug cast one — sample the local ground color, paint a soft low‑opacity shadow on a new layer and apply Gaussian blur, then reduce opacity to match.
6. Zoom in and check edges at 100% for artifacts; refine with a tiny brush.
7. Flatten or export a copy; keep the working PSD/XCF with layers in case you want further tweaks.

Photoshop / Photopea (best results)
- Duplicate the background layer.
- Make a loose selection around the mug (Lasso / Object Selection).
- Edit > Content‑Aware Fill (Photoshop) or Edit > Fill > Content-Aware (Photopea). Use the Sampling Brush to exclude areas you don’t want sampled (e.g., product edges).
- Set Output To: New Layer (Photoshop). Inspect result.
- Clean up with Spot Healing Brush / Patch tool / Clone Stamp on the new layer. For patterned backgrounds, use Clone Stamp with aligned sampling from adjacent areas.
- Recreate shadow on a new layer with a soft brush using sampled color, blur and reduce opacity as needed.

GIMP
- Duplicate layer.
- Use Free Select around mug or the Heal Selection (requires Resynthesizer plugin).
- If plugin available: Filters > Enhance > Heal Selection.
- Otherwise: use Clone tool and Healing tool to paint over the area using nearby pixels. Work in small steps and frequently sample nearby textures.
- Add or refine shadow on a new transparent layer if necessary.

Snapseed (mobile)
- Open image > Tools > Healing.
- Zoom in and paint over the mug in small strokes; Snapseed often needs multiple small passes.
- For leftover artifacts, undo and retry with smaller brush or alternate strokes from adjacent areas.
- Export a copy when satisfied.

Online automatic tools (fast, often good)
- cleanup.pictures, inpaint.online or Photopea (web) — open the image, use the brush to paint over the mug, click Remove/Erase.
- These give fast results but may need manual touchups afterwards for best fidelity.

Tips for preserving “everything else unchanged”
- Avoid sampling from across product edges — keep samples local to the background surface.
- If product is reflective or near the mug, pay attention to reflections; you may need to clone small reflection details.
- Preserve lighting: if the mug cast a shadow that overlapped the product, carefully reconstruct the product edge shadow (or remove shadow only from the floor, not the product).
- Work at full resolution and check at 100% to avoid softening fine edges.
- Save a layered file so you can revert or re-edit.

If you want:
- I can give a step‑by‑step tailored to one specific tool (Photoshop, Photopea, GIMP, Snapseed, or a particular online service).
- Or, if you upload the image and tell me which tool you’ll use, I can create a precise mask/inpainting instruction (e.g., exactly which area to paint/retain and any color samples for shadow recreation) for you or for an automated inpainting tool to use.

Which tool would you like instructions for, or would you like to upload the photo so I can produce a precise mask/inpainting plan?
